_label: PROVISIONAL template, NOT RUN on the 4x4080 server. ik_llama.cpp llama-server, GLM-5.3-Flash UD-Q4_K_XL (architecture string glm5next, which ik_llama loads: docs/reassessment/research/R2-engines.md:137). Flags are those of the command that ran on the 3x3090 host (scripts/run-glm-3090-1gpu.sh:29-34; PROBLEMS.md:105, pp 166.8 / tg 15.0 tok/s on 1x3090 there, REPORTED), changed for 4 GPUs: -sm layer and -ts instead of -sm none, -t/--threads-batch for the 48-core EPYC 7H43, KV f16 (ADR-012 D5) instead of q8_0. ik_llama's -sm graph does not support glm5next (R2-engines.md:116). Check every flag against `llama-server --help` of the ik_llama build on the server (artifacts/engine/flags_check.json); N12 ran this pin's CPU build with a tiny glm5next GGUF (CONFIRMED there, docs/evidence/2026-10-11-n12-ik-glm5next-cpu.md on branch claude/n12-ik-glm5next-cpu; not re-run here): /tokenize gives llama.cpp's ids but ignores with_pieces; ignore_eos and n_predict work; /v1/completions logprobs use llama.cpp's layout (what logprob_compare reads), /completion n_probs the old one; on a CPU build -ngl/-sm/-ts are absent from --help and -ts fails with one device (irrelevant on the GPU server). --help prints the usage to stdout and exits 1 (common/common.cpp:2716-2719 and 1016-1019, examples/server/server.cpp:480-482 @5194a9e, read here), hence help_ok_codes [0, 1]. For B1: ik does not compute the same function as llama.cpp's glm5-next (SwiGLU clamp after vs before SiLU, DSA tail slots padded with cell 0, indexer LayerNorm eps, expert_group_count not read for glm5next; N12), so differences between the two engines are expected even with correct kernels.

_notes.safety_rules: scripts/r1/safety_rules.py checks this file before any step (run_r1.py refuses a violating config, exit 2); the rules are section (v) of docs/reassessment/PHASE-CLOSE-2026-10-11.md, accepted by the owner, applied as configuration guards only (no upstream patch in the R1 build). Rule 1: --parallel 1 stays explicit (ik's own default is 1, common/common.h:323@5194a9e; the rule asks for it written out); no speculation in this template. Rule 2: --chat-template-file ${REPO}/templates/glm-5.3-flash/chat_template.jinja (ik supports the flag: common/common.cpp:2935 and :3454@5194a9e; N26a started this pin's CPU build with it and the template rendered without the reasoning leak, docs/evidence/2026-10-12-n26a-r1-safety-rules.md); model.chat_template_sha256 is checked and recorded. Rule 3: clients never send "reasoning_content": null; tools/gateway/gateway.py drops it. Rule 6: if slots are enabled later, restore only through tools/kv/session_store.py. Rule 8: no manifest yet, so model.weights_unverified_reason marks every run UNVERIFIED; a GGUF from the epyc-ai host only after tools/hostcheck/glm_gguf_check.sh. Rule 9: ik_llama.cpp is NOT a parity reference for GLM: differences from llama.cpp are expected even with correct kernels (6 differences, N12); until the SwiGLU experiment the default semantics is clamp BEFORE SiLU (PROVISIONAL, N24), which ik does not compute.
_notes.experiment: B1 row 'ik_llama.cpp, the same GGUF' (docs/reassessment/EXPERIMENTS.md); ik_llama pin 5194a9e (R2-engines.md:66)
_notes.IK_BIN: bin/ of the ik_llama.cpp build of scripts/engines/build_engine.py (/srv/llm/engines/current-ik_llama -> /srv/llm/engines-build/ik_llama.cpp); the commit is engine.pin = tools/engines/pins.json[ik_llama.cpp] (5194a9e14); step engine_build_check compares ${IK_BIN}/../build-info.json with the pin (sha, sm_89 cubins, sha256 of every built file) and does not start the engine on a mismatch. Build: python3 scripts/engines/build_engine.py --engine ik_llama.cpp --arch 89 --src-root /srv/llm/engines-src --build-root /srv/llm/engines-build
_notes.WEIGHTS_DIR: the UD-Q4_K_XL files: 6 shards, 185.983 GiB on the 3090 host (AGENTS.md); the choice of weights for the 4x4080 server is open (ADR-005/ADR-009), the HF revision and manifest are UNKNOWN here, so weights_verify is skipped until model.weights_manifest is set
_notes.NCMOE: PROVISIONAL: 17 of 42 MoE layers on the CPU, from the uniform-routing placement of tools/roofline.py (UD-Q4_K_XL, experts 4.89 bpw: resident 60.7% at 262144 tokens); tune on the server (the 3090 host used 39 of 42 with one 24 GB card)
_notes.HIT: PROVISIONAL: (42 - NCMOE) / 42 = 0.595 with uniform routing; keep it equal to the placement when NCMOE changes
_notes.bpw: experts 4.89 / dense 8.04 (PROVISIONAL, docs/reassessment/ROOFLINE.md table 2 for GLM UD-Q4_K_XL); replace with this run's quant_audit.json
_notes.mode: overlap no (as llama.cpp: tools/roofline.py decode() docstring), miss cpu (-ncmoe: the CPU computes its layers' experts)
_notes.THREADS: PROVISIONAL: 48 physical cores of the EPYC 7H43 (AGENTS.md); the 3090 host used -t 96 --threads-batch 90 on its own CPU
_notes.supports_slots: false: on the CPU build /slots save and restore work once --slot-save-path is given, and restoring the save of an EMPTY slot crashes the server (GGML_ASSERT src/llama.cpp:11739 @5194a9e; N12, reproduced twice there); slot_persist saves only after a completion. Add --slot-save-path ${SLOT_DIR} and set true after a check on the GPU build
_notes.INDEXER_KV_TYPE: the DSA indexer K-cache has its own type (-ictk, default f16 whatever -ctk is: common/common.h:495, common/common.cpp:2035-2037 @5194a9e); set it with KV_TYPE when K2 is meant to cover the indexer cache
